# Linguistic Metadata

Our genetic data was taken from a range of sources (see Supplementary Table X <!--# This will be a table of where the samples were taken -->). In each case. there was a variant of the question "What is your primary language?". In Y cases, language was inferred based on the location from which the sample was taken. All coding decisions on language names, locations, and the comparability of questions across samples are detailed in the script `processing/format_geneticdata.R`.

In the tables below, we list some summary statistics. A notable discrepancy is that there are more individuals with missing language families than missing languages. In three cases, respondents gave an answer of a language, but we cannot pair it to a language from existing databases. These are: Imani (n = 19), Eyagu (n = 1), and Kora (n = 1).

Linguistic decisions of note:

-   Paiwaian (n = 52) is a language which has disputed membership to TNG, and could also be considered as part of the Tereban family [@pawley2017]. We include this language as a branch of TNG.

<!-- -->

-   We have one speaker of Orokolo, an Eleman language that is sometimes categorized as a TNG language. @pawley2017 writes that there is no evidence for this link. We do not categories this language as TNG.

# Phylogenetic Results

## Genetic Data

This project leverages existing samples drawn from 14 papers, with an additional 7 unpublished samples. In total, we analyse a sample of 861 mitogenomes. See Supplementary Table XX for the original papers which details the sequencing technology used for each paper.

```{r}
#| echo: false

ref_count = TNG_metadata %>% 
  filter(!is.na(citation)) %>%
  group_by(citation) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  arrange(desc(n))

ref_count %>% 
  adorn_totals(where = "row") %>% 
  kable(col.names = c("Reference", "Sample count"))

```

### Duplicate mitogenomes

There are 190 individuals with duplicate mtDNA mutations that group in to 107 distinct sets (i.e. some individuals have identical mitogenomes to multiple people). Of the 107 duplicate sets, 53 matched pairs have mismatched language classifications.

For phylogenetic modelling, we do not include duplicate genomes, as the contain no additional information. We add duplicate tips back to the phylogeny after its construction in order to include individuals in subsequent analysis. Details of the adding tips procedure can be found in the script `adding_tips.R`

## Phylogenetic model

#### Mutation Rates

We use a strict clock mutation. We determine mtDNA mutations rates from studies calibrating the human mitochondrial clock (@rieux2014, @fu2013). In both studies we consider the whole genome substitution rate. We take the mean mutation rate from both papers to determine our rate.

|             Paper | Estimated Mean Mutation Rate |  Estimated 95% C.I.   |
|------------------:|:----------------------------:|:---------------------:|
|    Fu et al. 2013 |        2.67 x 10^-8^         | 2.16 - 3.16 x 10^-8^  |
| Rieux et al. 2014 |        2.143 x 10^-8^        | 1.58 - 2.706 x 10^-8^ |
|         Used here |       2.4065 x 10^-8^        |          \-           |

: {Mutation rates from existing studied #tbl-letters}

#### MCMC Settings

We run BEAST for 175,570,000 MCMC iterations, storing every 10,000 iterations. We take a burn-in of 20% which leaves us with a posterior sample of 14,047 trees, using the BEAST2 LogCombiner tool [@drummond2007]. All valuable parameters have an ESS \> 200. We create a Maximum Clade Credibility tree (MCCT) using the BEAST2 TreeAnnotator tool [@heled2013].

The bModeltest results show 44.41% support for a nucleotide substitution model of the form 123323. This is a non-traditional substitution model which contains distinct parameters for the A-C transition; A-G and C-T transversions; and third parameters for the G-T transition, and the A-T and C-G transversions.

```{r}
#| echo: false
log = read.table("NCI/20240910_CBESbModelTest_ALL/top.log",
                 header = TRUE,
                 skip = 1219)

# remove 20% burnin
burnin = ceiling(nrow(log) * 0.2)
log.noburnin = log[burnin:nrow(log),]

ggplot(data = log.noburnin, aes(x = Sample, y = posterior)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  ggtitle("MCMC Trace of the Posterior",
          "With burn-in removed") + 
  ylab("Posterior") + xlab("")
```

# Inference Results

### Walking Distance

We calculate distance between individuals as the cumulative time using Tobler's hiking distance. We then look at three increasing time barriers that map onto approximate distances of marriage according to @amato1983 (Table 1), which states that marriages range from between 1 and 186 kilometers away, with closer marriages being more common. Assuming a baseline of flatground walking, 66km takes around 12 hours. Using this as a baseline, we look at distances between individuals that are approximately 12 hours walk away, 24 hours walk away, and 48 hours (not including breaks for sleeping).

### Pairwise Between & Within group variance

We do not only want to understand the probability of particular histories, but also rate at which histories coalesce. To do this, for each pair we calculate the probability of between and within group variance to understand at what point, according to the phylogeny, were two languages groups likely to have been one language group.

This approach extends some assumptions of the phylogenetic model. First, that all partitions are binary.

```{r, wb_N, eval = TRUE, echo=FALSE}

trait = metadata_ss$TNG
names(trait) = metadata_ss$ID

v_within[,  generation_num := as.numeric(str_remove(generation, "g_")),]
```

# Genetic and Linguistic Distance

```{r}
## Data from Greenhill (In Press) - the TNG Phylogeny
tng_tree = read.nexus("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phlorest/greenhill_inpress/refs/heads/main/cldf/summary.trees?token=GHSAT0AAAAAACVQEUVFLA644VO6A2VDHQC4ZYEWJKQ")

tng_languages = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phlorest/greenhill_inpress/refs/heads/main/cldf/languages.csv?token=GHSAT0AAAAAACVQEUVFAUYKHVFWGUJB3IOAZYEWJUA")

# remove duplicates for merging
drop.langs = c("enga_wapi") # from ID
tng_languages = tng_languages %>% filter(!(ID %in% drop.langs))
tng_tree = drop.tip(tng_tree, "enga_wapi")

glottolog = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glottolog/glottolog-cldf/master/cldf/languages.csv")

## N and M metadata
# mcct_tree object used from earlier
metadata$ISO = str_extract(metadata$interview_language, "(?<=\\[)[a-z][^\\]\\[]*(?=])")
metadata_gl = left_join(metadata, glottolog[,c("Glottocode", "ISO639P3code", "Family_ID",
                                                "Latitude", "Longitude")], 
                       by = c("ISO" = "ISO639P3code"))

metadata_gl = left_join(metadata_gl, tng_languages[,c("ID", "Name", "Glottocode")], 
                       by = c("Glottocode"), suffix = c("", ".phy"))


language_distance = cophenetic.phylo(tng_tree)
dimnames(language_distance) = 
  list(tng_languages$Glottocode[match(tng_languages$ID,
                                         rownames(language_distance))],
       tng_languages$Glottocode[match(tng_languages$ID,
                                         colnames(language_distance))])

# geographic distance
geographic_distance = geosphere::distm(
  x = metadata_gl[,c("longitude_hybrid", "latitude_hybrid")]) / 1000
dimnames(geographic_distance) = list(metadata_gl$PhyID,
                                     metadata_gl$PhyID)

genetic_distance = cophenetic.phylo(mcct_tree)
genetic_distance[upper.tri(genetic_distance)] = NA
genetic_distance = reshape2::melt(genetic_distance, na.rm = TRUE)
colnames(genetic_distance) = c("Taxa1", "Taxa2", "genetic_distance")
genetic_distance$Language1 = metadata_gl$Glottocode[
  match(genetic_distance$Taxa1, metadata_gl$PhyID)]
genetic_distance$Language2 = metadata_gl$Glottocode[
  match(genetic_distance$Taxa2, metadata_gl$PhyID)]
genetic_distance$language_distance = NA
genetic_distance$geographic_distance = NA

for(i in 1:nrow(genetic_distance)){
  t1 = genetic_distance$Language1[i] %in% colnames(language_distance) # test1
  t2 = genetic_distance$Language2[i] %in% colnames(language_distance) # test2
  if(t1 & t2){
    genetic_distance$language_distance[i] = 
    language_distance[
      genetic_distance$Language1[i],
      genetic_distance$Language2[i]
    ]
    genetic_distance$geographic_distance[i] = 
    geographic_distance[
      as.character(genetic_distance$Taxa1[i]),
      as.character(genetic_distance$Taxa2[i])
    ]
  } else {
    genetic_distance$language_distance[i] = NA
  }
}

genetic_distance$same_langauge = genetic_distance$Language1 == genetic_distance$Language2

ggplot(genetic_distance, aes(x = genetic_distance, y = geographic_distance, 
                             col = same_langauge, size = language_distance)) + 
  geom_jitter()

ggplot(genetic_distance, aes(x = genetic_distance, y = language_distance, 
                             col = same_langauge)) + 
  geom_jitter()


```

```{r}
library(INLA)

genetic_vcv = ape::vcv(mcct_tree)
genetic_vcv <- genetic_vcv/max(genetic_vcv) 
genetic_vcv <- genetic_vcv / exp(determinant(genetic_vcv)$modulus[1] / nrow(genetic_vcv))

pcprior <- list(prec = list(prior="pc.prec", param = c(0.36, 0.1)))

gen_model <- inla(
  TNG_Branch ~ f(
    PhyID,
    model = "generic0",
    Cmatrix = genetic_vcv,
    constr = TRUE,
    hyper = pcprior
  ),
  data = metadata
)
```
